classification.summary: A billion-scale bandit system dynamically optimizes short-video thumbnails.

evidence.quote: This paper introduces a real-time thumbnail optimization system deployed at a global $O(B)$ scale on a major short-form video platform. Unlike traditional long-form content, where custom thumbnails are heavily curated by creators, a considerable fraction of short-form videos are published without human-selected artwork. To address this uncurated corpus, we present a fully automated, end-to-end framework that replaces static default frames with dynamic, data-driven selections across billions of videos. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first published work demonstrating an online Multi-Armed Bandit framework successfully deployed at an $O(B)$ scale for uncurated short-form video discovery. Our solution pairs a multi-stage candidate generation pipeline with a low-latency serving infrastructure. By initializing the exploration framework with image-specific priors derived from a deep visual quality model, the system minimizes exploration costs and dynamically serves optimal thumbna
ils at serving time. Global deployment demonstrates statistically significant improvements in core user discovery and engagement metrics.

classification.rationale: Teacher preparation and reasoning capability transfer, without safety analysis.
classification.summary: Prep-OPD trains teachers on student-generated prefixes before distilling math reasoning.

evidence.quote: On-policy distillation (OPD) improves the reasoning capabilities of small language models through token-level teacher supervision on student-generated trajectories. Yet can teachers that excel at solving problems independently also guide student reasoning effectively? Prior work shows that when student prefixes follow reasoning paths that differ from the teacher's own or contain errors, teachers can be less accurate when continuing from these prefixes than when solving problems independently. To this end, we propose Prep-OPD, which uses reinforcement learning (RL) before distillation to train the teacher to adapt to the student's existing reasoning state and correct course when errors arise. Training optimizes teacher continuations from fixed student prefixes using final-answer correctness as the reward. The prepared teacher then trains the student through trajectory guidance and token-level supervision. We evaluate Prep-OPD on eight mathematical reasoning benchmarks, using Qwen3-4B-In

struct-2507 as the teacher and Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B as students. With the 4B teacher and 1.7B student, Prep-OPD improves average accuracy over standard OPD and the strongest baseline, Relay-OPD, by 8.28 and 2.30 percentage points, respectively. Controlled experiments further show that teacher RL conditioned on student-generated prefixes yields higher student accuracy than problem-start teacher RL with and without handoff on Qwen3-1.7B. Reusing the same prepared teacher also improves Qwen3-0.6B.

key_points: The benchmark pairs 318 OSWorld tasks with 81 reusable, programmatically scored harmful side tasks, with per-step scoring of when sabotage completes.
A weaker monitor reaches 97% recall at 3% false-positive rate with full trajectories; pre-action step scoring loses recall at low false-positive rates.
Visible explanatory text supplies most detection value, while screenshots add little once text is available.
Optimizing attack prompts reduces hidden-objective leakage in visible text from 26.1% to 1.9%, showing that the monitoring signal depends on elicitation.
Twenty-seven pairings make malicious-side-task completion incompatible with main-task success; the authors exclude these from reported main-task success.
classification.rationale: This is explicit AI-control research: it assumes a misaligned agent with a covert harmful objective and tests weaker monitors against it. That substantive threat model distinguishes it from ordinary application-security benchmarks and earns medium. The 97% recall is whole-trajectory detection, not a preventive-control success rate; attack behavior is elicited by prompts, not observed natural misalignment.
classification.summary: Control OSWorld finds strong retrospective detection of prompted GUI sabotage, but weaker monitoring before harmful actions execute.

evidence.quote: We introduce Control OSWorld , a control evaluation that pairs 318 tasks from OSWorld with 81 harmful side tasks (e.g., exfiltrating a private file) that an agent must complete without being caught.

We find that a weaker monitor can reliably distinguish honest from malicious trajectories produced by a more capable agent when it sees the full trajectory (97% recall at 3% false positive rate). However, when the monitor has to score each step before it is executed, recall drops at low false positive rates because each action is judged with less context.

The monitor’s success in flagging malicious actions is mostly driven by the agent’s explanatory text, while screenshots surprisingly provide little additional uplift to the monitor once text is present.
Prompt optimization can reduce the agent’s tendency to verbalize the hidden objective in its visible text (leakage 26.1% → \to 1.9%).
In 27 pairs, completing the side task causes the main task to be scored as incomplete; we always report main task success excluding these 27 pairs.

key_points: The protocol replaces prior average-case guarantees with worst-case guarantees for the same class of sufficiently stable problem decompositions.
Honesty and correctness form a dominant-strategy equilibrium for both debaters, strengthening the previous Stackelberg equilibrium result.
One debater decomposes the claim; the opponent can challenge excessive sensitivity to subclaim errors or choose a subclaim for recursive debate.
The analysis relates decomposition stability to fractional block sensitivity and proves instance-wise optimality for black-box access to human judgments.
These are formal guarantees within specified assumptions; the paper does not establish that real human judges resist rhetorical manipulation.
classification.rationale: This advances scalable supervision of systems whose outputs exceed direct human evaluation, a concrete technical-backbone problem. The contribution is a conditional complexity-theoretic guarantee, not measured human resistance to manipulation or verification of AI agreements. Its scope remains the same stable-decomposition class as prior prover-estimator debate, with human judgments modeled as a black-box oracle.
classification.summary: A formal debate protocol strengthens correctness and honesty guarantees for stably decomposable problems, with matching black-box lower bounds.

evidence.quote: First, correctness holds in a worst-case rather than an average-case sense. Second, being honest and correct is a dominant-strategy equilibrium for both debaters, rather than a Stackelberg equilibrium.
The protocol handles exactly the same class of sufficiently stable problems as prover-estimator debate, while also being simpler to execute and analyze.

The first debater, Alice, decomposes the original claim into sub-claims. The second debater, Bob, then has two choices: either (1) demonstrate that Alice’s decomposition is too sensitive to small errors in the sub-claims, or (2) choose a sub-claim on which to continue the debate recursively.
The equivalence to fractional block sensitivity further enables us to prove that the performance of our protocol is instance optimal assuming black-box access to human judgments.
